rv.q: Goodman is magnificent in the central role.
A truly thought provoking, intelligent piece of theatre.
It's an evening of genuinely epic entertainment.

The comic moments work and it's always a pleasure to listen to George Tabori's translation as revised by Alistair Beaton, but – pace Goodman’s neatly delivered little envoi once he’s removed the moustache – there's no horror in the heart of this farce.

cn.t: Goodman's transformation from ridiculous buffoon to terrifying tyrant anchors this timely Brecht revival, though critics split on whether the character's evolution fully convinces. The production's contemporary resonance registers strongly.
